name: Sentry
one_liner: Error and performance monitoring platform with a documented REST web API and integration platform.
auth_notes: Bearer auth tokens from internal integrations or personal tokens; OAuth2 (auth code with PKCE, device flow) for public integrations. Region hosts (us/de) and self-hosted base URLs differ.
access_notes: Internal integrations and tokens are self-created under Settings > Developer Settings. Free Developer plan ($0) exists; pricing page lists 'API & third-party integrations' under the Team plan, so free-plan API limits are unverified.
sandbox_or_test_env: Free Developer plan ($0, one user) usable as a test org

buildability.rationale: Self-serve tokens and standard OAuth2, documented rate-limit headers, signed webhooks. Residual doubt: pricing page lists API under the paid Team plan; per-endpoint rate limits.

disputes.why: Tokens self-created in Developer Settings; $0 Developer plan exists. Caveat: Team plan lists 'API & third-party integrations'.
Integration platform webhooks with signed headers for issue, alert, error, comment resources.
Rate Limits page documents per-endpoint windows, concurrency limit and X-Sentry-Rate-Limit headers.

auth.quote: Internal integrations can only be used by your organization, whereas public integrations can be published and are available for all Sentry users.

access.quote: For solo devs working on small projects
In sentry.io, navigate to Settings > Developer Settings. From here, you can choose to create an internal or public integration.

api_surface.quote: Each endpoint has its own maximum number of requests and window size.
Sentry uses JSON webhooks to get error notifications to your systems or services.

mcp.quote: The base MCP server address is: https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp

buildability.quote: Polling the API for updates is likely to quickly trigger rate limiting. We recommend using our webhooks, if possible.

identity.quote: Sentry’s integration platform provides a way for external services to interact with Sentry using webhooks, UI components, and the REST API.
